{{Vanilla|Monster Spawner|Spawner}}
{{Infobox
|title=Spawner
|type=Block
|caption=Drops a divine fragment when broken
}}
A '''spawner''' (monster spawner) in [[Matcha Flavoured]] is worth breaking rather than farming. Breaking one drops a {{ItemLink|Divine Fragment}}, most mobs from the pack's spawners drop nothing, and putting a spawn egg on a spawner destroys every spawner nearby and hurts the player.

== Obtaining ==
Spawners can't be obtained as items in Survival. When broken, a spawner drops one {{ItemLink|Divine Fragment}}.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/spawner.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/treasure/divine_fragment.json}}</ref> Fortune doesn't increase the drop.

== Generation ==
The pack generates its own spawners in several structures:<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/worldgen/configured_feature/monster_room.json}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
! Structure !! Mob
|-
| [[Dungeon|Monster room]] || [[Zombie]], [[Skeleton]] or [[Spider]], with equal chances
|-
| [[Papal Outpost]] watchtower || [[Zombie]]
|-
| [[Woodland Mansion]] (one room) || [[Spider]]
|-
| [[Abbey]] rooms || [[Husk]], [[Skeleton]], [[Cave Spider]]
|}
Monster rooms are placed as a vanilla monster room followed by one of three spawner templates, <code>matcha:spawner/zombie_spawner</code>, <code>skeleton_spawner</code> or <code>spider_spawner</code>. Monster rooms are also more common than in vanilla; see [[Dungeon]].

== Behavior ==
=== Mobs drop nothing ===
The spawners placed by the pack's structures give their mobs the <code>NoDrops</code> tag. The zombie, husk, skeleton, spider and cave spider loot tables check for this tag and drop nothing when it is present.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/entities/zombie.json}}</ref> This makes spawner-based mob farms useless for loot.

Spawners generated by vanilla code rather than a structure template, such as those in mineshafts, strongholds and [[Nether Fortress|fortresses]], don't tag their mobs, so those mobs still drop their normal loot.

As with any hostile mob, spawner mobs are also subject to the [[Spawning#Surface check|surface check]]: after the [[Ender Dragon]] is killed, a spawner above Y=63 or open to the sky can only keep spawning inside trial chambers and abbeys. See [[Surface]].

=== Spawn eggs ===
If a player who is not in Creative mode uses a spawn egg on a spawner or a trial spawner:<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/no_egg_on_spawner.mcfunction}}</ref>
* every spawner and trial spawner within 16 blocks of the player is destroyed (using the <code>destroy</code> mode of <code>/fill</code>, which drops their loot);
* the player takes 20 damage ({{Hp|20}}), enough to kill a player with 10 hearts and no armor.

The check matches item IDs, not item names, so it also applies to the pack's items that are built on spawn eggs, such as the [[Bedrock Buster|bedrock buster]], {{ItemLink|Flour}}, {{ItemLink|Dough}}, {{ItemLink|Raw Diamond}}, {{ItemLink|Nazar}} and the curry stocks.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/no_eggs_on_spawners.json}}</ref>

== Trivia ==
* The README's tips for new players include "Break Spawners!".<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref>
* The design video explains that divine fragments, found "by vanquishing powerful forces or breaking spawners", are meant to discourage mob grinders: "You could make a simple mob grinder, but the divine fragment is staring you in the face."<ref>{{Cite video|quote=You could make a simple mob grinder, but the divine fragment is staring you in the face.}}</ref>
* The developer had wanted spawner mobs not to drop anything since before 1.12.2, but noted that "tag can't influence loot tables I dont think". The feature was added by HapppySpud.<ref>{{Source|changelog.md}}</ref>
